videos.script: A number in Java is never just a number. It has a type, and the type decides how big it can get. {{ranges}} This lesson starts with the eight primitive types, the ones built into the language. A program prints each one's size and limits. Two of them, int and double, are the ones you reach for by default. {{overflow}} Then the edge. Add one to the largest int and you get the smallest, with no error at all. {{boxing}} After that, the wrapper classes. Integer holds an int as an object, and Java converts between the two by itself. Two Integers holding 127 compare equal with two equals signs. Two holding 128 do not. You will see why. {{var}} Last, var. It looks like a variable with no type. It is a variable whose type the compiler wrote for you, and it still cannot change. By the end you can pick the right type for a value, and say what goes wrong at its limits.
